documents.text: Donald Macdonell (Upper Canada politician) Donald Macdonell (January 17, 1778 – June 13, 1861) was a political figure in Upper Canada. He was born in Greenfield, near Aberchalder, in Inverness-shire, Scotland in 1778, the son of Alexander Macdonell, and came to Charlottenburgh Township in Upper Canada in 1792 as part of a group of Scottish settlers led by his father. He studied with John Strachan in Cornwall. He served with the local militia during the War of 1812, reaching the rank of lieutenant-colonel.
